it allows up to five connections 
processor and memory are shared 
disk size is 256MB

and a new page to show the results of this web api endpoints
and to explain how to use the API endpoints 
there is no authentication needed to use these endpoints
the web api endpoint will accept http post 
and return a uuid-v7 guid or something 
and then the client will be able to get what they sent us with the guid with http get
if it still exists with us otherwise they will get a 404 not found

where clients can get aggregate all the data they have sent us 
based on their referer and their key

The Beacons API, the `/beacons` page and the storage clean-up are written, but I couldn't compile or run the C#: this sandbox has no .NET SDK and can't reach NuGet. The SQL did run correctly against a local PostgreSQL 16 (schema, totals, per-referer and hourly counts, multi-key counts, and the size-based delete). Please build it once (`dotnet build` / `dotnet run --project Zen.Blazor`) before you push.

Extract the archive at the repo root. It only contains files that changed or are new, and nothing needs deleting.

**Changed:** `README.md`, `.github/workflows/velixir.yml`, `Zen.Blazor/Program.cs`, `Zen.Blazor/Zen.Blazor.csproj`, `Zen.Blazor/appsettings.json`, `Zen.Blazor/Components/_Imports.razor`, and `MainLayout.razor` plus its `.css` (adds a Beacons link).
**New:** 16 files in `Zen.Blazor/Beacons/`, plus `Components/Pages/BeaconBoard.razor` and its `.css`.

**Endpoints** (no authentication, CORS open):

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/beacons/{key}` | Stores the request; returns 201 with a UUIDv7 id and a `Location` header |
| GET | `/api/entries/{id}` | Returns everything recorded, or 404 if it's gone |
| GET | `/api/beacons/{key}?referer=` | Totals, top referers, and hourly counts for the last 24 hours |
| GET | `/api/beacons/{key}/entries` | Lists entries, newest first, with paging |
| GET | `/api/beacons` | Busiest keys |
| GET | `/api/status` | Database and memory health |

**How it behaves:**
- **Requests:** bodies can be up to 32 KiB. Headers, body, referer, user agent, method, path and query are recorded. IP addresses are cut to /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), and `Cookie`, `Authorization` and forwarding headers are blanked out, because everything stored is publicly readable.
- **When the database is down:** writes land in a capped in-memory buffer (4 MiB) first, and a background writer saves them to Postgres in batches. If the database is down, reads use memory and say `degraded: true`. The writer keeps retrying, waiting longer each time up to 60 seconds. A lookup for an id that isn't in memory returns 503 with a `Retry-After` header instead of a false 404.
- **Staying under the 256 MB disk:**
  - Every 2 minutes, entries older than 30 days are deleted.
  - If stored data passes 48 MiB, the oldest entries are removed until it's back to about 80% of that.
  - If the whole database passes 160 MiB and is still growing, the 48 MiB limit is halved and the table is vacuumed.
  - All of these limits are settings in `appsettings.json`.
- **Connections:** each app instance opens at most 2 of the 5 database connections. It builds the connection from your `postgreshost`, `postgresport`, `postgresdatabase`, `postgresuser` and `postgrespassword` variables, and uses `postgresconnectionstring` only if those are missing. The table is created on first use.
- **Limits:** each IP can make 30 writes and 120 reads per minute.
- **Demo page:** `/beacons` counts visits, has four reaction buttons with live counts, and shows recent entries, top keys and copy-paste examples (curl, `sendBeacon`, CSP).
- **CSP demo:** every page now sends a report-only Content Security Policy. Violation reports go to the key `zen-csp`, so they also count against the storage limits.

**Upgrades:**
- Added Dapper 2.1.89 and Npgsql 10.0.3, the latest stable versions. Npgsql 10 targets .NET 10. These are the first third-party packages in the project.
- `actions/checkout@v7` was already the latest.
- I added a build job (`actions/setup-dotnet@v6`) that must pass before deploy. Pull requests now build but don't deploy.
- I removed the one comment that was in the workflow file.

Sources:
- [Npgsql on NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Npgsql)
- [Dapper on NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Dapper)
- [actions/checkout releases](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases)
- [actions/setup-dotnet releases](https://github.com/actions/setup-dotnet/releases)
- [Dapper + Npgsql `ANY(@array)`](https://dev.to/ankursheel/how-to-write-a-query-with-the-in-operator-using-dapper-and-npgsql-4cg0)

























































Claude
